question: Construct a gene co-expression network by computing pairwise Pearson correlation coefficients across genes, retaining only significant co-expression relationships where the absolute correlation |r|>0.6. Visualize the network with nodes sized by their degree, edge widths and edge transparency proportional to |r|, and highlight the hub genes with different color.

files.eval_guideline: Network graph must show nodes sized by degree, edge widths and edge transparency proportional to |r|, and hub genes (high-degree nodes) highlighted in a distinct color from non-hub nodes; layout, color scheme, and node label visibility may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files have the identical basename gene_coexpression_network.png and PNG image format, directly corresponding to the requested gene co-expression network visualization. Their paths also identify the same task, b-3-13.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires visual encodings of degree, correlation magnitude, and hub status while explicitly allowing layout, colors, and label visibility to vary. Semantic comparison can assess these graphical requirements without requiring pixel-level agreement.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images depict a gene co-expression network using |Pearson r| > 0.6, with node sizes representing degree, edge width and transparency representing correlation magnitude, and distinct colors identifying hubs. Both show a densely connected core with peripheral low-degree genes. Six highlighted hubs agree: Gene_01, Gene_03, Gene_11, Gene_18, Gene_26, and Gene_33. The reference additionally highlights Gene_02 and Gene_10 because it defines hubs as the top 20%, whereas the candidate uses degree at or above the 90th percentile (k ≥ 15). This changes hub classification but preserves the principal high-connectivity pattern. The candidate additionally reports 40 genes, 132 edges, 60 samples, and BH FDR < 0.05, labels all genes, and explicitly displays six isolated genes. These details are not established by the reference, whose unlabeled non-hub nodes make exact edge and node correspondence difficult to verify. The candidate identifies the displayed edges as positive correlations; the reference does not distinguish correlation sign, so sign agreement cannot be confirmed. Despite these qualifications, both satisfy the requested visual encodings and convey substantially the same scientific message. Layout, colors, and label visibility differences do not materially affect equivalence.
